open_points.subject: Which concurrent store changes a later backup must contain
open_points.text: “a change committed while the copy is made goes on, is not in this backup and is in the next” has no exception for agent-session changes, while rule 2 says every backup removes all agent sessions; it also does not say whether “the next” means the next run, the next kept backup, or the state that still exists when a later snapshot begins.
open_points.question: Which changes does the promise “is in the next” cover, and what exactly must a later backup contain when the changed state is deliberately excluded from backups or is changed again before the next snapshot?
options: It covers every committed store change, including agent-session changes, contradicting rule 2.
It covers only records backups retain, and only if their resulting state still exists at the next snapshot.
It promises preservation of the committed event itself, which would require history beyond the snapshot’s then-current records.
It means only that a later snapshot is eligible to observe the change, not that it must contain it.
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a snapshot-boundary statement only: a commit after the read transaction begins is excluded from that snapshot and may be reflected in the next kept snapshot only through whatever retained state exists then; agent sessions remain excluded.

witness.initial: Registry has a registered agent session S with access version 1, and a daily backup run has begun its read transaction.
events: The owner grants project P to S while the backup copy is being made; the grant transaction commits.
The current backup finishes and is kept.
The next daily run succeeds and keeps another backup.
The owner restores that next backup outside Registry.
outcomes: Under the new sentence, the committed grant is in the next backup, so restored session S has project P.
Under A18 rule 2, the next backup contains no agent session at all, so restored Registry has neither S nor its grant.
witness.observer: The owner after restoring the next backup, and Kernel when it tries to use or re-register session S.
